description: We are a multidisciplinary team that believes science is for everyone. We are driven to take ideas further, because we are convinced that a good solution can have multiple functionalities and help many people at the same time. We seek to make technology and science understandable, accessible, and useful in different scenarios, from space to everyday life. We don't just develop tools: we build bridges between science and people.
summary: ARTEMIS is an artificial intelligence agent and virtual companion designed to facilitate interactive monitoring of astronauts' health during their spaceflight. It assesses bone density by examining trabecular bone loss using confocal acoustic ultrasound (SCAN), estimating the bone volume fraction (BV/TV) with attenuation parameters (BUA) and sound speed (SOS). Its physiological stress and circadian rhythm module analyzes salivary cortisol via chemiluminescence (CLIA/ECLIA), adjusting its thresholds to the exact time of the sample and the individual’s profile. In response to radiation exposure, it processes TEPC detector readings, classifying environmental risk into three categories: instantaneous dose and daily cumulative dose. Likewise, the mental and cognitive health module does not rely on physical sensors and implements interactive sleep tracking, objective reaction time tests (PVT-B), workload assessment (NASA-TLX), and a daily mood check. Artemis synthesizes the information into a three-level traffic-light system (Green, Yellow, and Red) and issues immediate behavioral recommendations, alerts to the flight physician, and autonomous, personalized recommendations for the mission. In addition, ARTEMIS can also be used by people on Earth who need to monitor these metrics (bone density, radiation, and stress).
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?
ARTEMIS is an artificial intelligence agent and interactive virtual companion designed for autonomous monitoring and self-regulation of astronauts' health during space missions. The system operates by articulating four fundamental biomedical pillars:
· Bone density: Evaluates the microstructure of the calcaneus through Scanning Confocal Acoustic Navigation (SCAN). It uses a combined linear regression model that integrates Broadband Ultrasound Attenuation (BUA) and Ultrasound Velocity (SOS/UV) to estimate Bone Volume Fraction (BV/TV) and detect accelerated loss in microgravity.
· Physiological stress and circadian rhythm: Analyzes salivary cortisol concentrations through chemiluminescent immunoassays (CLIA/ECLIA). Its algorithms evaluate the sample in relation to the exact time of collection and the time since waking.
· Radiation exposure: Processes real-time readings from the TEPC (Tissue-Equivalent Proportional Counter) detector, evaluating environmental risk in three layers: instantaneous rate, accumulated daily dose, and career limits.
· Mental and cognitive health: Integrates a morning sleep log, the objective 3-minute Psychomotor Vigilance Test PVT-B, the NASA-TLX workload assessment, and a Daily Mood Check (CDA).
All information is synthesized into three-level traffic lights (Green, Yellow, and Red), and ARTEMIS issues alerts and recommendations when it detects anomalies, such as tactical naps, exercise protocols, and notifies when safety limits are exceeded. It also offers the option of exporting structured data to feed biomedical research.

2. What benefits does it offer?
· Physiological and Operational in Space: Helps prevent acute bone deconditioning (losses of 1% to 2% per month), avoids overexposure to radiation peaks, and reduces the risk of human error due to cognitive fatigue in critical missions.
· Medical autonomy in orbit: Allows the crew to self-assess their physical and mental state without depending on on-site diagnoses from Earth or being affected by communication delays.
· Useful platform for scientific research: Allows all recorded biomedical and cognitive data to be easily exported and downloaded (in standardized formats such as PDF or JSON) for subsequent statistical analysis and medical research.
· Terrestrial applicability: In addition to its function in space, SCAN ultrasonic technology and its normative tables facilitate bone density analysis on Earth, allowing non-invasive evaluation of osteopenia and osteoporosis in elderly people.

3. What is the expected impact?
· Reduction of operational risk in space: Prevents human errors derived from cognitive fatigue and mitigates acute bone deconditioning and overexposure to radiation.
· Mitigation of social desirability bias: By acting as a private and confidential coach rather than a prescriptive medical surveillance system, it eliminates the fear of operational disqualification and encourages sincere self-reporting.
· Impact and transfer to health on Earth: Provides an accessible model for bone density screening in older adults and monitoring of personnel in extreme terrestrial environments (commercial aviation, submarines, oil platforms, and Antarctic bases).

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?
· Development tools: Open Code (main development environment), Visual Studio Code, GitHub, npm/Node.js (frontend dependency management).
· Infrastructure and technological hosting: GitHub Cloud (repository and version control).
· Backend and API: Python, FastAPI, SQLModel, Pydantic, SQLite, i18n.
· Frontend and interface: React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML5, CSS3, react-i18next (es/en internationalization), custom SVG vector graphics, 3-step registration assistant, main HUD with the interactive A.R.T.E.M.I.S. agent, and SummaryCards.
· Programming languages: Python (50%), TypeScript (35.6%), CSS (13%), JavaScript (1.2%), HTML (0.2%).
· AI and machine learning: Interactive A.R.T.E.M.I.S. agent, advanced statistical models (linear regressions, log-normal distributions, and Sleep Regularity Index), domain mathematical engines.
· Software and design: Open Code, Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, pytest, bilingual i18n (es/en) in backend and frontend.

5. In what sense is your project creative?
· Monitoring agent: ARTEMIS facilitates astronaut health monitoring and communicates recommendations and alerts clearly.
· Anti-habituation evolving interface: Didactic capsules adapt across three levels of depth (full explanation, summary, or prescription only).
· Dual-use approach (Space/Earth and Research): Integrates interactive monitoring with export facilities for scientific research and the adaptation of bone density analysis for elderly people on Earth.

6. What factors did your team take into account?
· Simple understanding: Astronaut data results are visualized simply and, above all, clear alerts are sent and recommendations are offered.
· Physiology in microgravity (0 g): The influence of the spaceflight context on alert thresholds for astronaut data.
· Space environment conditions: The absence of 24-hour light/dark cycles, orbital radiation peaks.
· Clinical and research scalability: The need to have easily downloadable data to drive scientific studies and adapt bone density analysis to fracture prevention in the terrestrial geriatric population.
